name: Moksy on Meta
description: Using Facebook and Instagram ads in line with Moksy's documented economics, positioning, content motion, brand rules and claims.

cards.subject: Moksy's price range
says: is £19 to £79 a month
makes revenue a volume number rather than a few large deals
cards.use: need to judge a cost of winning a customer against what Moksy charges
not: is a single annual fee of several thousand pounds

cards.subject: The £100k-a-year subscriber count
says: is roughly 280 to 440 paying subscribers at Moksy's prices
shows why Moksy's revenue depends on volume
cards.use: are asked how many subscribers a £100k year takes
not: is roughly 20 to 40 large contracts

cards.subject: The outbound-sales conclusion
says: holds that outbound sales cannot reach the volume Moksy needs
describes Moksy's growth as a content and search problem
cards.use: hear a suggestion to grow Moksy by hiring a sales team
not: concludes that paid social is the main growth channel

cards.subject: The documented growth motion
says: is guides and search shipped at one guide a week
tracks free Blueprint started and Pro upgrade by landing page
cards.use: need to describe how Moksy's own documents say it should grow
not: is built around paid social from the start

cards.subject: Paid social's status at Moksy
says: is absent from the documented growth motion
makes any Facebook or Instagram test a new test
must earn its place against the same numbers as the guides
cards.use: are asked whether Meta ads are part of Moksy's plan
not: is a documented channel with agreed targets

cards.subject: A £19 subscriber's annual value
says: is £228 in a year before churn and costs
sets a ceiling on what can sensibly be paid to win one subscriber
cards.use: need a ceiling for what to pay to acquire a Pro-priced subscriber
not: is £19 once, with no recurring revenue

cards.subject: The 4, 8 and 12 week review
says: looks at results at 4, 8 and 12 weeks
follows the chain impressions, clicks, Blueprints, Pro
cards.use: need to schedule when a guide's results are judged
not: judges every guide after the first week

cards.subject: The four-to-eight-week wait
says: expects nothing for four to eight weeks after a guide ships
explains that judging earlier measures the crawler's schedule, not the content
cards.use: are tempted to judge a new guide after a few days
not: expects results within 48 hours

cards.subject: The guide diagnosis rule
says: reads impressions without clicks as a title problem
reads clicks without Blueprints as a close problem
cards.use: see a guide with impressions but few clicks
not: reads impressions without clicks as a pricing problem

cards.subject: Moksy's one-line description
says: reads: Idea in, build-ready plan out
says AI structures the idea and vetted experts refine it
cards.use: need the product described in one line
not: describes Moksy as a software agency

cards.subject: The only-voice-not-selling-the-build position
says: is the central position in Moksy's SEO document
rests on every other ranking page belonging to an agency that wants the build
makes neutrality Moksy's entire advantage
cards.use: need the reason a reader should trust Moksy's cost guidance
not: rests on Moksy having the cheapest builders

cards.subject: The never-recommend-a-builder rule
says: applies even to a sister company
stops Moksy pointing readers to a particular agency
cards.use: are tempted to name a favourite builder in a guide
not: allows recommending a sister company

cards.subject: The ranges-as-ranges rule
says: labels ranges as ranges
labels cost ranges as agency marketing
cards.use: need to present a cost range from the market
not: treats a range as the reader's own number

cards.subject: The sourced-figures rule
says: states only figures that appear in a source
forbids interpolating numbers to look more precise
cards.use: are asked to add a precise-looking number with no source
not: allows rounding an unsourced guess to look tidy

cards.subject: The guide ending
says: tells the reader a range is not their number
points to the free Blueprint as the way to get their own number
is an honest conversion because it is what the product does
cards.use: are writing the close of a Moksy guide
not: ends with a request to book a call with an agency

cards.subject: The saturated head term
says: is held by agencies with years of links
is not fought by Moksy
cards.use: are asked whether Moksy should chase the biggest cost keyword
not: is the main place Moksy expects to win quickly

cards.subject: The winnable gap
says: lies between having an idea and signing an agency
favours high-intent questions with weak current answers and a direct line to the product
cards.use: need to pick which questions to target first
not: lies in the broadest cost keyword

cards.subject: The Moksy name
says: is written with a capital M
cards.use: are proofreading ad copy that spells the product name
not: is written in all lower case

cards.subject: The current tagline
says: is Turn your idea into a build-ready plan
ends with a full stop
cards.use: need the tagline for a headline or footer
not: is Empowering your digital transformation

cards.subject: The retired-taglines list
says: names three older taglines that must not appear
includes AI requirements + expert review
cards.use: find an old tagline in a draft ad
not: includes Turn your idea into a build-ready plan

cards.subject: Blueprint
says: is the document Moksy produces
replaces the retired word report
cards.use: need the name of the document a customer receives
not: is the retired word for the guided conversation

cards.subject: Briefing
says: is the guided conversation
replaces the retired word interview
cards.use: need the name of the guided conversation
not: is the document Moksy produces at the end

cards.subject: The retired-words list
says: names report, interview and pillars as words not to use
cards.use: see the word report in a draft ad
not: names Blueprint and Briefing as words not to use

cards.subject: The spine
says: runs Idea, Briefing, Blueprint, Review, Build
puts Review after the Blueprint
cards.use: need the order of the Moksy journey
not: runs Build, Review, Idea, Blueprint, Briefing

cards.subject: The Title Case rule
says: applies to headings and buttons
contrasts with sentence case for body copy
cards.use: are writing a headline and a button label
not: applies to body copy

cards.subject: The ALL-CAPS rule
says: allows ALL-CAPS only through the eyebrow style
rules out ALL-CAPS headlines
cards.use: are tempted to shout a headline in capitals
not: allows ALL-CAPS in any headline for emphasis

cards.subject: The spelling rule
says: requires British English
cards.use: are choosing between colour and color in ad copy
not: requires American English

cards.subject: Moksy's voice
says: is friendly, professional and confident
uses plain language
cards.use: need the tone for ad copy
not: is playful and slang-heavy

cards.subject: Brand orange
says: is #EF4123
is the only non-neutral action colour
cards.use: need the colour for the main call to action
not: is used for every status message

cards.subject: The one-primary-action rule
says: allows one primary action per view
stops several buttons competing for attention
cards.use: are placing buttons on a landing screen
not: gives every button the primary style

cards.subject: Status colours
says: are for state, not decoration
are kept apart from the action colour
cards.use: are tempted to use a red or green accent as decoration
not: serve as the main action colour

cards.subject: Moksy's imagery style
says: is minimal and icon-led
cards.use: are choosing the look of an ad image
not: is busy collage photography

cards.subject: Product and data visuals
says: are preferred to stock photography
cards.use: are choosing between a stock photo and a product screen
not: are avoided in favour of stock photography

cards.subject: Decorative image alt text
says: is empty
keeps screen readers from announcing ornamental images
cards.use: add a purely decorative image to a page
not: describes the picture in a full sentence

cards.subject: Meaningful image alt text
says: is descriptive
tells a screen reader user what the image conveys
cards.use: add an image that carries information
not: is left empty

cards.subject: The evidence rule for ads
says: limits ads to what exists and can be evidenced
treats every ad as a claim
cards.use: are drafting an ad that mentions a capability
not: allows describing planned features as available

cards.subject: Ad figures
says: must come from a source
follow the same editorial rule as the guides
cards.use: want to put a number in an ad
not: can be estimated if they sound credible

cards.subject: Facebook sign-in
says: is listed in the integrations plan as existing
is gated by environment settings
cards.use: are asked whether Facebook sign-in can be mentioned
not: is listed as absent from the product

cards.subject: Facebook Page import
says: is listed as absent in the integrations plan
would use the Graph API with pages_show_list and pages_read_engagement
would need Meta's App Review
should not be promised in an ad unless that has changed
cards.use: are asked to advertise importing a Facebook Page
not: is already live and ready to advertise

cards.subject: The guest-quota caution
says: comes from a launch promo proposal dated 13 August 2026
says guest AI quotas reset when a new session is minted
says a guest or free offer should not be pushed with paid traffic until fixed
cards.use: are asked to push a guest or free offer with paid traffic
not: is a settled decision that needs no checking

cards.subject: Expert Review values
says: are published in MOX as reviewer-facing job values
can change
are already included in Pro and Max
cards.use: are tempted to quote what a review is worth in an ad
not: are fixed customer prices safe to quote

cards.subject: The ad's permitted promise
says: is the free Blueprint
cards.use: need to decide what an ad may offer
not: is a free expert review

cards.subject: Moksy's six starting points
says: name a booking system, an e-commerce website, a SaaS MVP, a marketplace, a school website and a mobile app
cards.use: need the project types Moksy builds guides around
not: are Founders, Teams and startups, Agencies, Enterprise, Education and Public sector

cards.subject: Moksy's audience pages
says: are Founders, Teams and startups, Agencies, Enterprise, Education and Public sector
cards.use: need the audiences on the public site
not: are a booking system, an e-commerce website and a marketplace

cards.subject: The ad-to-guide match
says: sends an ad about a starting point to the guide for that starting point
avoids a generic landing page
cards.use: are choosing the destination for an ad about booking systems
not: sends every ad to the home page

cards.subject: Wave 1 guides
says: number eight and include the software cost hub
are all linked from /resources/guides
cards.use: need to know which guides exist first
not: number six and include the SaaS MVP and marketplace guides

cards.subject: Start free
says: is the one primary call to action everywhere
cards.use: need the call to action on an ad's button or page
not: is used on the home form only

cards.subject: Get my Blueprint
says: is used on the home form only
cards.use: are asked where Get my Blueprint belongs
not: is the primary call to action everywhere

cards.subject: The landing-page dimension
says: splits free Blueprint started and Pro upgrade by landing page
is the only number that says whether a page earns its place
cards.use: need to know which page deserves the credit for a signup
not: adds all signups into one total

cards.subject: Low click-through on a Moksy ad
says: points at the ad's hook
cards.use: see an ad with a low click-through rate
not: points at the landing page's close
like: High click-through with few Blueprint starts

cards.subject: High click-through with few Blueprint starts
says: points at the landing page's close
cards.use: see an ad with many clicks but few free Blueprint starts
not: points at the ad's hook
like: Low click-through on a Moksy ad

cards.subject: Measuring Moksy's ad events
says: would need Meta's pixel or Conversions API
depends on consent rules deciding whether events may fire
cards.use: need to see free Blueprint started attributed to an ad
not: works without any tracking on the site

cards.subject: A campaign
says: holds the advertising objective
contains one or more ad sets
cards.use: need to set what the advertising is trying to achieve
not: holds the individual images and videos people see

cards.subject: An ad set
says: holds the audience, placements, budget and schedule
sits between the campaign and its ads
cards.use: need to change who sees the ads or how much is spent
not: holds the campaign objective

cards.subject: An ad
says: is the creative a person actually sees
sits at the lowest level of the structure
cards.use: need to change the image, copy or button people see
not: sets the audience for a group of campaigns

cards.subject: A placement
says: is a place an ad can appear, such as Feed, Stories or Reels
can be chosen automatically or manually
cards.use: need to control where an ad shows
not: is the audience an ad is shown to

cards.subject: A daily budget
says: sets an average amount to spend each day
lets delivery vary day to day
cards.use: want spend to continue at a steady rate without an end date
not: fixes a total spend over the whole schedule

cards.subject: A lifetime budget
says: fixes a total to spend over the set dates
paces spend across a schedule with an end
cards.use: need to spend a set total by a known end date
not: sets an average for each day

cards.subject: A campaign-level budget
says: shares one budget across the ad sets in a campaign
lets delivery favour the ad sets with better results
cards.use: want delivery to move spend between ad sets automatically
not: gives each ad set a fixed separate budget

cards.subject: Structure consolidation
says: keeps fewer ad sets so each gathers enough results to learn
avoids splitting budget across near-identical audiences
cards.use: find budget spread thinly across many near-identical ad sets
not: adds a separate ad set for every interest

cards.subject: Ad account roles
says: control who can create or edit ads
apply least privilege to people and agencies
cards.use: need to give an agency access without letting it change billing
not: let every user edit every setting

cards.subject: The awareness objective
says: aims to reach people likely to remember the ad
suits a brand people do not yet know
cards.use: want a new brand remembered by as many people as possible
not: optimises for purchases

cards.subject: The traffic objective
says: aims to send people to a destination such as a website
can attract clickers who never take a next step
cards.use: want more visits to a page
not: optimises for contact details

cards.subject: The engagement objective
says: aims for interactions such as reactions, comments and shares
builds social proof on a post
cards.use: want more reactions and comments on a post
not: optimises for installs

cards.subject: The leads objective
says: aims to collect contact details or enquiries from interested people
suits businesses that follow up with prospects
cards.use: want enquiries from interested people to follow up
not: optimises for reach alone

cards.subject: The sales objective
says: aims for purchases or other valuable conversions
relies on conversion tracking to learn who converts
cards.use: want the delivery system to find people who buy or sign up
not: optimises for video views

cards.subject: The app promotion objective
says: aims for installs and actions inside a mobile app
cards.use: want people to install a mobile app
not: aims for contact form submissions

cards.subject: The optimisation event
says: is the action delivery tries to get more of
can differ from the business outcome that matters
cards.use: are choosing which action an ad set should optimise for
not: is the reporting window for results

cards.subject: Objective mismatch
says: happens when the objective optimises for an easier action than the real goal
produces cheap clicks that never convert
cards.use: see cheap results that never become customers
not: happens when the budget is too large

cards.subject: A proxy event
says: stands in for a rarer action when too few real ones occur
trades some relevance for enough volume to learn
cards.use: find the real conversion happens too rarely for delivery to learn from it
not: is the final outcome the business cares about

cards.subject: A core audience
says: is built from demographics, location and interests
cards.use: want to reach people by who they are and what they like
not: is built from your own customer list

cards.subject: A custom audience
says: is built from your own data such as customers, visitors or engagers
cards.use: want to reach people who already know you
not: finds strangers resembling a source group

cards.subject: A lookalike audience
says: finds new people who resemble a source audience
depends on the quality of its source
cards.use: want new people similar to your best customers
not: contains only people who have already visited your site

cards.subject: Retargeting
says: re-engages people who already interacted with you
speaks to people who know the offer
cards.use: want to follow up with people who viewed a page but did not sign up
not: finds people who have never heard of you

cards.subject: An exclusion
says: keeps a defined group out of delivery
stops existing customers seeing acquisition ads
cards.use: want current customers not to see an offer for new ones
not: adds extra people to an audience

cards.subject: Broad targeting
says: leaves the audience wide and lets delivery find responders
puts more weight on the creative
cards.use: want delivery to find responders with few constraints
not: narrows delivery with many interest layers

cards.subject: Interest targeting
says: reaches people by topics they have shown interest in
cards.use: want to reach people by subjects they follow
not: reaches only people on your customer list

cards.subject: Audience overlap
says: occurs when ad sets compete for the same people
can raise costs by bidding against yourself
cards.use: find two ad sets reaching mostly the same people
not: happens when an audience is too small to deliver

cards.subject: A source audience
says: defines whom a lookalike resembles
should reflect the outcome you value, not any click
cards.use: are choosing the group a lookalike is built from
not: limits the countries an ad can show in

cards.subject: Audience saturation
says: occurs when a small audience has seen the ads so often that results fall
calls for new creative or a wider audience
cards.use: see results fall as the same small group sees the ads again and again
not: occurs when two ad sets target the same people

cards.subject: A single image ad
says: pairs one picture with text and a button
cards.use: want the simplest static format
not: lets people swipe through several cards

cards.subject: A video ad
says: uses motion to tell a story in a short time
cards.use: want to show a product working
not: is limited to one still picture

cards.subject: A carousel ad
says: shows several swipeable cards, each with its own media and link
cards.use: want to show several products or steps in one ad
not: shows one picture with one link

cards.subject: Primary text
says: is the main copy above the media
cards.use: want to write the longer message above the picture
not: is the short bold line beside the button

cards.subject: A headline
says: is the short bold line near the call to action button
cards.use: want a short line that sits close to the button
not: is the main copy above the media

cards.subject: A call-to-action button
says: is a labelled button chosen from a preset list
cards.use: want a clear next step beside the ad
not: is free text written anywhere in the image

cards.subject: A hook
says: is the opening moment that earns attention
decides whether people keep watching or scrolling
cards.use: find that people leave an ad within its first moments
not: is the closing offer at the end of the ad

cards.subject: Vertical full-screen formats
says: fill the screen in Stories and Reels style placements
need key content clear of interface overlays
cards.use: are making creative for Stories and Reels
not: are limited to wide landscape media

cards.subject: Sound-off design
says: makes a video understandable with captions and visuals alone
cards.use: expect many people to watch without audio
not: depends on a voice-over to carry the message

cards.subject: Dynamic creative
says: combines supplied media and text into variations automatically
shows which combinations perform
cards.use: want delivery to mix several images and headlines for you
not: tests one hand-built variable at a time

cards.subject: A creative concept
says: is a distinct idea or angle, not a recolour of the same ad
cards.use: are planning a test of genuinely different approaches
not: is a change of button colour

cards.subject: An A/B test
says: splits the audience into non-overlapping groups to compare versions
gives a cleaner comparison than watching two live ad sets
cards.use: want a fair comparison of two versions
not: lets the same people see both versions

cards.subject: A single-variable test
says: changes only one thing between versions
lets you attribute a difference to that change
cards.use: want to know which element caused a difference
not: changes headline, image and audience together

cards.subject: A hypothesis
says: states what you expect to change and why before the test runs
cards.use: are planning a test and want it to teach something
not: is written after seeing the results

cards.subject: Test duration
says: runs long enough to cover a full weekly cycle
avoids stopping on one unusually good day
cards.use: are deciding when to stop a test
not: ends the moment one version leads

cards.subject: A primary metric
says: is chosen before the test starts
decides which version counts as the winner
cards.use: are choosing what result will decide a test
not: is picked after the results are in

cards.subject: Statistical significance
says: indicates a difference is unlikely to be due to chance alone
cards.use: are asked whether a small gap between two ads is real
not: proves the winning ad will keep winning

cards.subject: Creative fatigue
says: is a decline in response when the same people see an ad repeatedly
is addressed with fresh creative
cards.use: see response drop for an ad that has run a long time
not: is caused by a campaign objective being wrong

cards.subject: Iteration
says: builds the next test on what the last one showed
cards.use: have finished a test and need to plan the next
not: repeats the same test unchanged

cards.subject: Peeking
says: is ending a test early because of a lucky lead
inflates the chance of picking a false winner
cards.use: are tempted to stop a test after a promising first day
not: is waiting for a full cycle before deciding

cards.subject: A confounded test
says: changes several things at once so the cause is unclear
cards.use: cannot tell why one version beat the other
not: changes exactly one element

cards.subject: Impressions
says: count how many times an ad was shown
can include several views by the same person
cards.use: need the number of times an ad appeared
not: count the unique people who saw an ad

cards.subject: Reach
says: counts the unique people who saw an ad
cards.use: need to know how many different people saw it
not: counts every time the ad appeared

cards.subject: Frequency
says: is the average number of times each person saw an ad
equals impressions divided by reach
cards.use: want to know how often a typical person saw an ad
not: is the number of unique people reached

cards.subject: CPM
says: is the cost of one thousand impressions
cards.use: want to compare the price of attention across audiences
not: is the cost of a single click

cards.subject: Click-through rate
says: divides clicks by impressions
shows how well an ad earns the click
cards.use: want to know how compelling the ad was to those who saw it
not: divides conversions by clicks

cards.subject: CPC
says: is the cost of a single click
cards.use: want the price of each visit sent
not: is the cost of one thousand impressions

cards.subject: Conversion rate
says: divides conversions by clicks or visits
shows how well the destination closes the visit
cards.use: want to know how well the landing page finishes the job
not: divides clicks by impressions

cards.subject: Cost per acquisition
says: divides total spend by the number of conversions
cards.use: want the price of each signup or sale
not: divides revenue by spend

cards.subject: Return on ad spend
says: divides attributed revenue by ad spend
cards.use: want to know how much revenue each unit of spend returned
not: divides spend by the number of conversions

cards.subject: An attribution window
says: sets how long after an ad interaction a conversion can be credited to it
changes the reported results without changing real behaviour
cards.use: find two reports disagree on conversions for the same period
not: limits how long an ad can run

cards.subject: Customer acquisition cost
says: is the total cost of winning one new customer
has to be compared with what that customer is worth
cards.use: want the all-in cost of a new customer
not: is the revenue a customer brings

cards.subject: Lifetime value
says: estimates the total value of a customer over the whole relationship
sets how much it makes sense to pay to acquire one
cards.use: want to know how much a customer is worth in total
not: is the cost of winning one customer

cards.subject: Incrementality
says: asks whether conversions happened because of the ads
is measured against a control group that did not see them
cards.use: suspect that ads are claiming credit for sales that would have happened anyway
not: counts every conversion that follows an ad view

cards.subject: The Meta pixel
says: is code on a site that reports visitor actions to Meta
runs in the visitor's browser
cards.use: need to report page actions from the browser to Meta
not: sends events from a company server

cards.subject: The Conversions API
says: sends events to Meta from a server
is less affected by browser restrictions than browser code
cards.use: need to report events from your own server
not: runs only as code in the visitor's browser

cards.subject: Event deduplication
says: prevents one action being counted twice when browser and server both send it
relies on a shared event identifier
cards.use: send the same event by both pixel and server
not: blocks all events from the browser

cards.subject: Consent
says: decides whether tracking may fire
has to be respected before events are sent
cards.use: need to know whether an event is allowed to fire for a visitor
not: is a setting that raises ad quality

cards.subject: A standard event
says: is a predefined action name such as a purchase or a lead
lets reports and optimisation recognise common actions
cards.use: want to report a common action in a form delivery recognises
not: is a free-form note on an ad

cards.subject: UTM parameters
says: tag landing page links so analytics shows the source of a visit
cards.use: want your analytics to show which ad sent a visitor
not: send conversion events to Meta from a server

cards.subject: Ad review
says: checks ads against advertising standards before and during delivery
cards.use: submit an ad and wait for it to go live
not: happens only after a user complaint

cards.subject: Misleading claims
says: are forbidden in advertising
include promising results the product does not deliver
cards.use: are tempted to promise an outcome you cannot guarantee
not: are allowed if the small print explains them

cards.subject: Substantiation
says: requires evidence for objective claims before they run
cards.use: want to state a fact about the product in an ad
not: is only needed after an ad is reported

cards.subject: Landing page match
says: requires the destination to deliver what the ad promised
cards.use: are sending people from an ad to a page
not: allows a different offer on the page

cards.subject: Personal attributes
says: is the principle against implying you know sensitive facts about a person
rules out copy that says you know someone's health or finances
cards.use: are writing copy that addresses the viewer's circumstances
not: encourages naming a viewer's condition in the headline

cards.subject: Special ad categories
says: restrict targeting options for sensitive areas such as housing, employment and credit
cards.use: are advertising in a category with limited targeting
not: apply only to the largest advertisers

cards.subject: Brand safety controls
says: limit the kinds of content next to which ads can appear
cards.use: want to avoid ads appearing beside sensitive topics
not: decide which audience sees the ad

cards.subject: Comment moderation
says: hides or answers unwanted comments on ads
protects the brand where people can reply publicly
cards.use: find spam or abuse under a live ad
not: happens automatically with no setup

cards.subject: Partnership labels
says: disclose that content is a paid collaboration with a creator
cards.use: work with a creator who is paid to promote you
not: are optional when the creator is well known

cards.subject: Third-party rights
says: require permission for music, images and marks you do not own
cards.use: want to use a song or a photo you found online
not: are waived when credit is given

cards.subject: Repeated violations
says: can lead to restrictions on an ad account
make a clean record worth protecting
cards.use: find several ads disapproved for the same reason
not: are cleared whenever a new ad is made

cards.subject: The ad auction
says: decides which ad is shown by weighing bid, estimated action rates and ad quality
means the highest bid alone does not win
cards.use: want to understand why a lower bid can win an impression
not: is a fixed price list set by the platform

cards.subject: The learning phase
says: is the period when delivery is still working out who responds
can restart after significant edits
cards.use: have just launched or substantially edited an ad set
not: is a fixed week during which ads are paused

cards.subject: A bid strategy
says: controls how delivery spends to meet a cost goal
cards.use: are choosing how delivery should spend your budget
not: decides which creative is approved

cards.subject: A cost cap
says: tries to hold average cost per result near a limit
can cause underspend when the limit is too low
cards.use: want to keep average cost per result near a ceiling
not: guarantees every result costs below the limit

cards.subject: Scaling
says: raises budget gradually rather than in big jumps
protects the stability of results
cards.use: want to spend more on a campaign that works
not: is a single large budget jump

cards.subject: Ad quality
says: reflects signals from people as well as the bid
is part of how the auction values an ad
cards.use: find a rival wins impressions with a lower bid
not: is decided only by the size of the budget

cards.subject: Estimated action rate
says: is the auction's prediction of whether a person will take the optimised action
cards.use: want to know how the auction anticipates a click or conversion
not: is the cost reported after the ad ran

cards.subject: Underspend
says: happens when constraints leave the budget unspent
can come from a tight cost cap or a narrow audience
cards.use: find that an ad set fails to spend its budget
not: happens when the budget is too small to enter the auction

qa.q: Which level of a Meta ad account holds the audience, placements, budget and schedule?
qa.right: The ad set
qa.why: The campaign holds the objective, the ad set holds delivery settings, and the ad holds the creative.

qa.q: What is the price range Moksy's SEO document gives for the product?
qa.right: £19 to £79 a month
qa.why: The SEO document gives £19 to £79 a month, which makes revenue a volume number.

qa.q: Which spelling should appear in Moksy ad copy?
qa.right: Colour, with British English throughout
wrong: Either, as long as the ad is consistent
qa.why: Moksy's brand rules require British English.

qa.q: What does click-through rate divide?
qa.right: Clicks by impressions
qa.why: Click-through rate shows how often an ad that was shown earned a click.

qa.q: Which word should Moksy ad copy use for the document the product produces?
qa.right: Blueprint
qa.why: The document is a Blueprint; report is a retired word.

qa.q: Moksy's documented growth motion is built around what?
qa.right: Guides and search, shipped at one guide a week
wrong: Paid social from the first week
qa.why: The SEO document calls growth a content and search problem.

qa.q: Which call to action is the one primary call to action everywhere on Moksy?
qa.right: Start free
qa.why: Get my Blueprint is used on the home form only.

qa.q: A person sees your ad three times. Which metric counts that as one?
qa.right: Reach
qa.why: Reach counts unique people; impressions would count three.

qa.q: Which tagline is Moksy's current one?
qa.right: Turn your idea into a build-ready plan.
qa.why: The other three are retired taglines.

qa.q: Which campaign objective best fits wanting enquiries to follow up?
qa.right: Leads
qa.why: The leads objective aims to collect contact details or enquiries.

qa.q: Why does Moksy's document say outbound sales cannot reach the target?
qa.right: At £19 to £79 a month, revenue is a volume number
wrong: Outbound is not allowed under platform rules
qa.why: Roughly 280 to 440 subscribers are needed for £100k a year.

qa.q: What does a lookalike audience depend on most?
qa.right: The quality of the source audience
wrong: The size of the daily budget
The number of ads in the ad set
qa.why: A lookalike finds people resembling its source, so a poor source gives poor matches.

qa.q: Which Moksy colour is the only non-neutral action colour?
qa.right: Brand orange, #EF4123
qa.why: Status colours are for state, not decoration.

qa.q: A team tests a new image, a new headline and a new audience in one ad set against the old version. What is the problem?
qa.right: The test is confounded, so the cause of any difference is unclear
wrong: The test needs a larger budget
The test has too few placements
qa.why: Change one variable at a time so a difference can be attributed.

qa.q: A Moksy ad has a high click-through rate but few free Blueprint starts. Where should the team look first?
qa.right: The landing page's close
qa.why: Many clicks mean the hook works; few starts point at the close.

qa.q: A Moksy ad has a low click-through rate. Where should the team look first?
qa.right: The ad's hook
qa.why: Low click-through points at the ad's hook.

qa.q: A marketer wants an ad about booking systems. Where should it send people?
qa.right: The guide for booking systems
qa.why: Ads aimed at a starting point should go to that starting point's guide.

qa.q: A subscriber on £19 a month pays how much in a year before churn and costs?
qa.why: £19 multiplied by 12 is £228, which sets a ceiling on what can sensibly be paid to win one.

qa.q: Which is the better use of an exclusion on an acquisition campaign?
qa.right: Keeping existing customers out of the audience
qa.why: Exclusions stop people who have already converted seeing acquisition ads.

qa.q: Why choose the primary metric before a test starts?
qa.right: So the winner is not picked after seeing results that flatter a favourite
wrong: So the test runs for less time
So the platform can skip review
So the budget can be doubled
qa.why: Choosing afterwards invites bias.

qa.q: What does the Conversions API do?
qa.right: Sends events to Meta from a server
wrong: Sets the budget across ad sets
qa.why: It complements browser code and is less affected by browser restrictions.

qa.q: A report shows 40 conversions in one view and 55 in another for the same week. What is the most likely cause?
qa.right: Different attribution windows
qa.why: The window changes what can be credited to ads.

qa.q: A team asks to advertise importing a Facebook Page into Moksy. What should you do?
qa.right: Decline, because the integrations plan lists the Page import as absent
wrong: Run it and fix the product later
Mention it only in the comments
qa.why: Ads may only describe what exists and can be evidenced.

qa.q: Someone wants to quote what an Expert Review is worth in an ad. What is the best response?
qa.right: Do not, because the values are reviewer-facing and can change, and Pro and Max include reviews
wrong: Quote the MOX value as a price
qa.why: The ad's promise is the free Blueprint.

qa.q: A colleague wants to push a guest or free offer with paid traffic. What caution does Moksy's launch promo proposal raise?
qa.right: Guest AI quotas reset on a new session, so spend is uncapped until it is fixed
wrong: Free offers are banned by Meta
Free offers can only run on Reels
Guests cannot reach the landing page
qa.why: It is a proposal dated 13 August 2026, so check whether it still holds.

qa.q: A draft ad says 'Get your Moksy report in minutes'. Which two issues does it have?
qa.right: It uses the retired word report and states an unsourced timing
wrong: It uses a capital M and Title Case
It uses British spelling and a button
It names a Blueprint and a Briefing
qa.why: Copy must say Blueprint, and figures must come from a source.

qa.q: An ad set stops spending after a team sets a very low cost cap. What most likely happened?
qa.right: Delivery could not find results at that price, so it underspent
qa.why: A cap that is too tight leaves budget unspent.

qa.q: Two ad sets with near-identical audiences compete in the same auction. What is the remedy?
qa.right: Consolidate them or exclude one audience from the other
qa.why: Overlap makes you bid against yourself and splits learning.

qa.q: A team sends the same event from the pixel and from the server and sees doubled conversions. What is missing?
qa.right: Event deduplication with a shared event identifier
qa.why: Deduplication lets Meta count the action once.

qa.q: A small audience's results fall after weeks of the same ads. Which step fits best?
qa.right: Refresh the creative or widen the audience
qa.why: Frequency has grown and the audience is saturated.

qa.q: A team wants to scale a winning campaign. Which approach is safest?
qa.right: Raise the budget gradually and watch results
qa.why: Large jumps can disturb delivery.

qa.q: A cheap traffic campaign produces visits but no Blueprint starts. What is the likely cause?
qa.right: Objective mismatch, since it optimises for clicks rather than the real goal
wrong: The ad was approved too quickly
The lifetime budget was too high
The ad has too many placements
qa.why: Choose an optimisation event that is closer to the outcome.

qa.q: Which statement about Meta ads in Moksy's plan is accurate?
qa.right: They are not part of the documented motion, so any test has to earn its place
wrong: They are banned by the brand rules
qa.why: The SEO document's motion is guides and search.

qa.q: A guide has impressions but few clicks. According to the SEO document, what does it need?
qa.right: A better title
qa.why: Clicks without Blueprints would point at the close instead.

qa.q: A creator is paid to post about your product. What must you do?
qa.right: Disclose the partnership with the platform's label
wrong: Nothing, if the creator is independent
Hide the arrangement in the comments
qa.why: Paid collaborations must be disclosed.

qa.q: Why is it unwise to judge a new Moksy guide's search results after a few days?
qa.right: It measures the crawler's schedule, not the content
wrong: The guide is hidden for a week
qa.why: The document expects nothing for four to eight weeks.

qa.q: A report credits ads with many conversions, but sales stayed flat when ads were paused. What does this suggest?
qa.right: The ads were claiming credit for conversions that would have happened anyway
wrong: The attribution window was too short
qa.why: Incrementality asks whether conversions happened because of the ads.

qa.q: A test is stopped on day two because version B leads. What risk was taken?
qa.right: A false winner, because early leads are often chance
qa.why: Run to a full cycle to avoid peeking.

qa.q: Which design gives the best evidence that an ad lifts signups?
qa.right: A holdout group that does not see the ads
qa.why: A control group measures what would have happened anyway.

qa.q: Cost per acquisition looks good, but customers churn quickly. Which metric corrects the picture?
qa.right: Lifetime value compared with acquisition cost
qa.why: A cheap customer who leaves fast may not earn back the cost.

qa.q: A Moksy paid test shows a cost per Pro subscriber above what that subscriber pays in a year at £19 a month. What should the team conclude?
qa.right: The test fails against the ceiling unless other value justifies it
wrong: The test succeeds because clicks were cheap
The audience should be narrowed further
qa.why: £228 a year before churn and costs is the ceiling on what can sensibly be paid.

qa.q: A team wants a number to make a cost guide look precise but has no source. What does Moksy's rule say?
qa.right: Leave it out, because only sourced figures are stated
qa.why: Nothing should be interpolated to look precise.

qa.q: An ad for a school website cites a price. Which check comes first?
qa.right: Whether the figure appears in a source
wrong: Whether it fits in the headline
qa.why: Figures in ads must come from a source.

qa.q: Which Moksy brand check would an all-caps headline fail?
qa.right: The ALL-CAPS rule, which allows capitals only in the eyebrow style
qa.why: Headings use Title Case.

qa.q: A lookalike audience built from every clicker performs poorly. What is the likely fix?
qa.right: Rebuild it from people who completed the valuable action
qa.why: The source should reflect the outcome you value, not any click.

qa.q: An ad's image shows a stock photo of smiling people. Which Moksy rule does it conflict with?
qa.right: The preference for minimal, icon-led imagery and product visuals
wrong: The rule on the primary action
qa.why: Product and data visuals are preferred to stock photography.

qa.q: Which button label belongs on the Moksy home form only?
qa.right: Get my Blueprint
qa.why: Start free is the primary call to action everywhere else.

qa.q: A decorative divider appears in an ad landing page. What alt text should it have?
qa.right: Empty alt text
qa.why: Decorative images have empty alt text.

qa.q: Which Meta tool reports page actions from a visitor's browser?
qa.right: The Meta pixel
qa.why: The pixel runs in the browser.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT in the Moksy journey spine?
qa.right: Retarget
qa.why: The spine runs Idea, Briefing, Blueprint, Review, Build.

qa.q: A consent banner is declined by a visitor. What should happen to tracking events?
qa.right: They should not fire if consent rules say they may not
wrong: They are sent as server events instead
qa.why: Consent decides whether events may fire.

qa.q: A video ad is mostly watched with the sound off. Which fix helps?
qa.right: Add captions and make the visuals carry the message
qa.why: Sound-off design makes the video understandable without audio.

qa.q: An ad promises a free tool, but its landing page only sells a paid plan. Which principle is broken?
qa.right: Landing page match
qa.why: The destination must deliver what the ad promised.

qa.q: Why is the gap between an idea and a signed agency the winnable ground for Moksy's guides?
qa.right: Questions there have high intent, weak current answers and a direct line to the product
wrong: The head term is easy to win
Agencies do not write about costs
qa.why: The head term is saturated by agencies with years of links.
